fullPassage:
What does it mean to be brave? There is no single definition, but everyone is brave in their own way. Here are three young people sharing their bravest moments in life.

Jason
One evening, I went to a convenience store to buy some snacks. No one was at the counter, so I thought the clerk was working in the back. The telephone started ringing, but no one came to answer it. I felt something was wrong. I looked over the counter and saw the clerk lying on the floor. I immediately called 911 and explained the situation. The operator asked me to perform CPR on the clerk until the paramedics arrived. I was scared, but I remembered learning CPR at school. I started to push down on his chest, hoping that I was doing it right. A few minutes later, the paramedics rushed in and took over the situation. Luckily, the clerk regained consciousness. After putting the clerk in the ambulance, the paramedics said "Thank you for being brave. You did a wonderful job." It felt great to help save someone's life!

Olivia
I dreamed of being an Olympic track and field athlete. My room was full of medals and awards from races I had competed in. During the national 100-meter championship race, however, my Olympic dreams came to a sudden end. I was about to take the lead in the race when I suddenly felt a pain in my knee. I fell to the ground and had to be carried off the track. At first, I didn't think much of the injury. I thought I would get better soon. But the test results from the hospital were not hopeful. The doctors said my knee injury would prevent me from running again.

Every night, I had flashbacks of my injury. I could not watch sports anymore because it was just too painful. So I shut out everything related to sports from my life. Two years passed and I was still trying to get used to my ordinary high school life without sports. Then one day, I came across an interesting university major called sports medicine. It deals with the treatment and prevention of sports injuries. A light bulb went on in my head. This was my chance to stop running away from my problems and fears. So I made up my mind and applied to this major. Today, thanks to my brave decision, I am studying to be a star on the sidelines instead of on the playing field.

Yuna
Ever since I was young, I have admired great public speakers. I hoped to inspire and move audiences like them someday. But every time I had a chance to speak in front of people, I would get scared. I didn't want to make a fool of myself. This fear kept me behind the stage rather than on it. That's why I never entered the annual speech contest at my school. I really wanted to, but I just didn't have enough courage. Last year, however, was my final chance before graduating from high school. When I saw the poster on the class board, my mind began to fill with thoughts of the school speech contest. I heard a voice growing louder in my head, saying "Go for it!" I decided to sign up for the contest. To make a long story short, I did it. I delivered my speech to the entire school. How did I do? Honestly, I don't remember much from the contest because I was so nervous. But my act of courage taught me a valuable lesson: I can do anything that I put my mind to.

questions.passage: One evening, I went to a convenience store to buy some snacks. No one was at the counter, so I thought the clerk was ①<u>working</u> in the back. The telephone started ringing, but no one came to answer it. I felt something was wrong. I looked over the counter and saw the clerk ②<u>lying</u> on the floor. I immediately called 911 and ③<u>explaining</u> the situation. The operator asked me to ④<u>perform</u> CPR on the clerk.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 편의점에 갔다. 점원이 뒤에서 ①일하고 있다고 생각했다. 점원이 바닥에 ②누워 있었다. 911에 전화를 걸어 상황을 ③설명했다. CPR을 ④수행하라고 요청했다.
det.analysis: ❌ ③ explaining → explained: 'called 911 and explained' 병렬 구조. called(과거)와 같은 과거형. ✅ ① working: was working 정상. ✅ ② lying: saw+O+-ing 정상. ✅ ④ perform: asked me to perform 정상.
det.tip: 병렬 구조: A and B는 같은 형태. called and explained (과거+과거)

questions.passage: I dreamed of being an Olympic track and field athlete. My room was full of medals and awards from races I had ①<u>competed</u> in. During the national 100-meter championship race, however, my Olympic dreams came to a sudden end. I was about to take the lead in the race when I suddenly ②<u>felt</u> a pain in my knee. I fell to the ground and had to be ③<u>carried</u> off the track. But the test results from the hospital ④<u>was</u> not hopeful.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 올림픽 선수가 꿈이었다. 출전했던 경기에서 ①획득한 메달과 상으로 가득했다. 무릎에 통증이 ②느껴졌다. 트랙 밖으로 ③옮겨져야 했다. 검사 ④결과는 희망적이지 않았다.
det.analysis: ❌ ④ was → were: 주어 'the test results'가 복수 → were. ✅ ① competed: 과거완료 정상. ✅ ② felt: 과거형 정상. ✅ ③ carried: 수동태 정상.
det.tip: 주어-동사 수일치: results(복수) → were. 단수면 → was

questions.passage: So I shut out everything related to sports from my life. Two years passed and I was still trying to get used to my ordinary high school life without sports. Then one day, I came across an interesting university major ①<u>called</u> sports medicine. It deals with the treatment and prevention of sports injuries. This was my chance to stop ②<u>to run</u> away from my problems and fears. So I ③<u>made</u> up my mind and applied to this major. Today, thanks to my brave decision, I am studying to be a star on the sidelines instead of on the ④<u>playing</u> field.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 스포츠 관련된 모든 것을 차단했다. 스포츠 의학이라는 ①불리는 전공을 알게 되었다. 고민에서 ②도망치는 것을 멈출 기회였다. ③마음을 먹고 지원했다. ④경기하는 필드 대신 사이드라인에서 공부 중이다.
det.analysis: ❌ ② to run → running: 'stop -ing'(~하는 것을 멈추다). 'stop to V'(~하기 위해 멈추다)와 의미 다름. ✅ ① called: 과거분사(~라 불리는). ✅ ③ made: 과거형 정상. ✅ ④ playing: playing field 정상.
det.tip: stop -ing: ~하는 것을 멈추다 / stop to V: ~하기 위해 멈추다

questions.passage: I was about to take the lead in the race when I suddenly felt a pain in my knee. I fell to the ground and had to be carried off the track. At first, I didn't think much of the injury. But the test results from the hospital were not ①<u>hopeful</u>. The doctors said my knee injury would ②<u>encourage</u> me from running again. det.analysis: ❌ ② encourage(격려하다): 원문은 prevent(막다). 부상이 달리기를 '막는다'가 맥락에 적절. ✅ ① hopeful: 희망적인 정상. ✅ ③ flashbacks: 회상 정상. ✅ ④ painful: 고통스러운 정상.

위 글에서 구급대원이 Jason의 어떤 점에 감사했는지 본문에서 한 단어로 **영어**로 쓰시오.

"구급대원들은 Jason이 __________ 것에 감사했다."

det.korean: 구급대원들은 '용기를 내 줘서 고맙습니다'라고 말했다.
det.analysis: 'Thank you for being brave'에서 brave가 핵심.
det.tip: brave: 용감한

questions.passage: I was scared, but I remembered learning CPR at school. I started to push down on his chest, hoping that I was doing it right. A few minutes later, the paramedics rushed in and took over the situation.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 Jason이 학교에서 배운 것을 본문에서 **영어**로 찾아 쓰시오.

"Jason은 학교에서 __________ 배운 것을 기억해 냈다."

※ 약어로 쓸 것

det.korean: 겁이 났지만 학교에서 CPR을 배운 기억이 났다.
det.analysis: 'remembered learning CPR at school'에서 CPR이 핵심.
det.tip: CPR: cardiopulmonary resuscitation (심폐소생술)
